UGC NET (assistant professor, JRF)

Master's degree with at least 55 percent marks for general-category candidates, per a Careers360 summary of the NTA rules. Paper 1 has 50 questions for 100 marks. Paper 2 (geography) has 100 questions for 200 marks. Qualifying marks are 40 percent (general) and 35 percent (reserved). JRF has an age cap of 30, with relaxations.
A bachelor's alone does not qualify. Plan the master's first.
UPSC Civil Services

Geography is one of the optional subjects. In UPSC's 2023-24 annual report, as summarised by Physics Wallah, geography had 1,260 Mains takers and 94 selected (7.5 percent). One aggregator reported about 933 vacancies for the 2026 cycle.
The optional is a choice, not an advantage by itself.
Survey of India (surveyor posts)

Published 2013 rules: Surveyor Senior (Group B) asks for a B.Sc with maths, 60 percent (50 percent for SC and ST), direct-recruit age 21 to 28. Surveyor Junior (Group C) asks for Intermediate with maths, 60 percent. Officer Surveyor (Group B, gazetted) is filled 100 percent by promotion.
A BA without maths does not meet these rules. A B.Sc with maths does.
NRSC (ISRO)

March 2024 notice for temporary research posts: Project Associate-I asked for an M.Sc in Remote Sensing or GIS with a B.Sc in any subject. Research Scientist posts asked for an M.Sc in Geology or Applied Geology with physics, maths or geology at B.Sc, or an M.E. or M.Tech in remote sensing and GIS with a B.E. or B.Tech. No post named geography.
A geography graduate reaches NRSC through a remote sensing and GIS master's, not through the geography degree alone.
IIRS free online courses

A Careers360 article lists four free courses: Remote Sensing and GIS (4 weeks), Geospatial Applications (2 weeks), Space Technology Applications (6 weeks), Basics of Remote Sensing (1 week). A certificate needs 70 percent attendance, and students must also pass an online exam.
A free, credible way to test whether you like spatial work before paying for a course.
M.Plan at CEPT (urban planning)

2026-27 admissions: a four-year bachelor's including Geography among listed fields, at least 50 percent (45 percent reserved). A CEPT PG Test, GATE or UGC NET score is mandatory. 132 seats. The detailed list of eligible degrees names M.A. or M.Sc. Geography.
Geography is plausible, but confirm in writing whether a bachelor's in geography is accepted.
UGC NET (assistant professor, JRF)
ugcnet.nta.nic.in. For the December 2026 cycle, Careers360 lists applications from 8 to 28 October 2026 and exams from 14 to 19 December 2026. Confirm on the NTA notice.
Survey of India (surveyor posts)
surveyofindia.gov.in. Rules have been revised since 2013, so read the current advertisement.
IIRS free online courses
iirs.gov.in. The article does not give a batch year or seat count.
Civil services
Prelims, Mains and interview, repeated across attempts, with a low selection rate for every optional.
After selection, a pay scale and cadre. Growth is by seniority and posting, not by anything you can scale yourself.
Teaching and research
A master's with the required marks, then NET or JRF.
A funded PhD seat, then a permanent post. NET qualification does not give either.
Space and remote sensing
An eligible degree: a remote sensing and GIS master's for project posts, an engineering degree for most scientist posts.
The 2024 posts were temporary. A permanent role is a separate selection.
Urban planning
An entrance score (CEPT PG Test, GATE or NET at CEPT) for a limited number of seats.
Entry into planning firms and authorities. Ask any course for its last placement list and the roles in it, not an average.

figures.source: Watch out In UPSC's 2023-24 annual report, 1,260 Mains takers had geography as the optional and 94 were selected. That is 7.5 percent of that group.

supporting: The ownership path: a small GIS or mapping practice. It scales because you set the price per project, repeat work comes from the same clients and local bodies, and you can later hire a junior or use AI tools for the repeat steps. India's National Geospatial Policy 2022 opened the way for private entities to produce and use geospatial data, and a published explainer of the policy cited a projection of about 63,000 crore rupees by 2025 with more than 10 lakh jobs.

On pay: Payscale (February 2026, 25 profiles) shows an early-career GIS analyst average of about 3.9 lakh rupees a year, with a 10th-to-90th percentile range of about 1.9 to 8.3 lakh rupees. That is a small sample of self-reported early-career figures across employer types, so use it as a rough anchor. The top of the range is a strong result, not what most freshers see.
